ChatGPT, as tokens

Every value on this page is a CSS custom property generated from tokens.json (recaptured 2026-10-17 after ChatGPT's redesign): the primitive ramps and type, spacing, radius, size and motion scales in core, and the two palettes in light and dark, each with its role colours, variants, shadows, elevation, measured component values and the checklist roles. The Dark toggle flips data-theme on <html>, as ChatGPT does on .chatgpt-theme. Where a section shows both themes side by side, each half carries its own data-theme, so it ignores the toggle.

The interface font is the system stack in fontFamily.sans (SF Pro on Apple platforms). Nothing is loaded from the network: OpenAI Sans is proprietary and falls back to the system face. Only the Blue accent was captured, so the accent tokens below are Blue's. The drawings are rebuilt from the tokens; the real pixels are in screenshots/ and components/crops/.

Colour roles

The checklist roles (role.bg, role.text, role.border, role.accent) point into ChatGPT's own names (token.*, surface.*, text.*, variant.*). Each swatch shows where the alias lands. Light and dark sit side by side.

Contrast

The text and fill pairs the interface actually draws, with the WCAG 2 ratio worked out from the rendered colours (translucent fills composited over role.bg.page). AA needs 4.5 for body text, 3 for large text and for a focus ring against its ground.

Light

role.text.disabled resolves to the same grey as role.text.tertiary in both themes; ChatGPT draws placeholders with it.

Ramps

Each theme carries its own 25-step grey (gray.*), which runs white to black in light and flips in dark, so gray.0 is always the ground. core holds the fixed ramps: color.gray-fixed and seven hues from 25 to 1000.

Four status triples, each a fill, a text colour and a border, plus a solid colour for dots and filled badges. They alias the surface and solid variants of the matching hue.

Variant matrix

ChatGPT's Button and Badge read variant.<colour>.<style>.*. Each cell shows rest, hover, active and the focus ring (ring) for that pair. This section follows the Dark toggle.

A blank state falls back to the one before it (hover to rest, active to hover); a pair with no text takes soft.text of the same colour. secondary has no surface style.

Type

One family for the interface: the system stack. Every composite in typography.* is rendered in its own style; letter spacing, which the font shorthand cannot carry, comes from its sibling property.

Spacing, radius and size

The spacing unit is 4px (spacing.unit); the steps are multiples of it, named like Tailwind (spacing.1_5 is 6px). Rows and pills are fully round, cards 24, menus 16.

Focus ring

A keyboard focus draws a ring in role.border.focus (ring.default) at size.focusRing.width with size.focusRing.offset, as a box-shadow. Rows and tabs draw it inset. Each pair is rest, then focus-visible; tab through the page to see the live ones.

Elevation

elevation.* names a shadow by what it lifts: a control, a card, a menu, a tooltip, a dialog, a drawer, a modal, the composer. Most alias the shadow.* scale; the tooltip and dialog are raw layers. Values below are the active theme's.

The whole shadow.* scale

Motion

Colour and opacity changes run 150ms (duration.basic) on easing.default; larger moves use the enter curves. Press Play to run every track; the curves are drawn from the cubic-bezier values.

Thread

Compare the two shortest-path algorithms and show me the code.

Both find shortest paths from one source. Dijkstra needs non-negative weights and runs in O((V + E) log V) with a heap; Bellman-Ford allows negative edges and reports a negative cycle, at O(VE). See the lecture notes.

At a glance

AlgorithmNegative edgesTime
DijkstraNoO((V + E) log V)
Bellman-FordYesO(VE)

Code

python
# relax every edge V - 1 times
def bellman_ford(graph, start):
    dist = {v: float("inf") for v in graph}
    dist[start] = 0
    for _ in range(len(graph) - 1):
        for u, v, w in graph.edges():
            dist[v] = min(dist[v], dist[u] + w)
    return dist
